title: A Taylor polynomial from a table, with two error bounds

stimulus.title: Values of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> and its derivatives
stimulus.html:
The function hh has derivatives of all orders for x>−1x > -1. The table gives values of hh and its first three derivatives at x=0x = 0 and x=1x = 1. The fourth derivative of hh is h(4)(x)h^{(4)}(x)=960(x+1)6= \frac{960}{(x + 1)^6}. The Taylor series for hh about x=1x = 1 is ∑n=0∞(−1)n(n+1)(x−1)n2n−1\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n (n + 1)(x - 1)^n}{2^{n-1}}, and it converges to h(x)h(x) for −1<x<3-1 < x < 3.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the third-degree Taylor polynomial P3(x)P_3(x) for hh about x=1x = 1.

rubric.point: First three terms from the values at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 - 2(x - 1) + \frac{3}{2}(x - 1)^2</annotation></semantics></math>

Cubic term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{-6}{3!}(x - 1)^3</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -(x - 1)^3</annotation></semantics></math>, with the polynomial ending there (no "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mo>⋯</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \cdots</annotation></semantics></math>")

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use P3(x)P_3(x) to estimate h(1.2)h(1.2).

rubric.point: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(1.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - 0.4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>0.06</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.008</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 0.06 - 0.008</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.652</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.652</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx P_3(1.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - 2(0.2)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.04</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0.008</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{3}{2}(0.04) - 0.008</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2 - 0.4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mn>0.06</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.008</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 0.06 - 0.008</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.652</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.652</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the Lagrange error bound to show that |h(1.2)−P3(1.2)|<1500\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right| < \frac{1}{500}.

rubric.point: The largest value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h^{(4)}(z)\right|</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le z \le 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>960</mn><mn>64</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(4)}(1) = \frac{960}{64} = 15</annotation></semantics></math>, with a reason: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>960</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{960}{(z + 1)^6}</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing on that interval
accept: "<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(z + 1)^6</annotation></semantics></math> increases, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>960</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{960}{(z+1)^6}</annotation></semantics></math> is largest at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z = 1</annotation></semantics></math>"

rubric.point: Lagrange error bound written: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right| \le \frac{15}{4!}(0.2)^4</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\max|h^{(4)}|}{4!}|1.2 - 1|^4</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max = 15</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: Evaluates the bound, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.0016</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{15}{24}(0.0016) = \frac{1}{1000}</annotation></semantics></math>, and concludes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>500</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1000} < \frac{1}{500}</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(4)}(z)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>960</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{960}{(z + 1)^6}</annotation></semantics></math> is positive and decreasing for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>></mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z > -1</annotation></semantics></math>, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(z + 1)^6</annotation></semantics></math> increases. So on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le z \le 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> the largest value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h^{(4)}(z)\right|</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>960</mn><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(4)}(1) = \frac{960}{2^6} = 15</annotation></semantics></math>. By the Lagrange error bound, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right| \le \frac{15}{4!}|1.2 - 1|^4</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.0016</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{15}{24}(0.0016)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0.001</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>500</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{1000} < \frac{1}{500}</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Explain why the alternating series error bound can be used for the estimate in part (b), and use it to find a bound on |h(1.2)−P3(1.2)|\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right|. Can the alternating series error bound be used in the same way to bound |h(0.8)−P3(0.8)|\left|h(0.8) - P_3(0.8)\right|? Explain.

rubric.point: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> the terms of the Taylor series, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(-1)^n (n + 1)(0.2)^n}{2^{n-1}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (-1)^n \cdot 2(n + 1)(0.1)^n</annotation></semantics></math>, alternate in sign, and their sizes decrease and approach 0
accept: sizes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.06</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.008</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.001</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2, 0.4, 0.06, 0.008, 0.001, \ldots</annotation></semantics></math> shown decreasing with limit 0

rubric.point: The bound is the first omitted term (<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 4</annotation></semantics></math>): <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5(0.2)^4}{2^3} = \frac{1}{1000}</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right| \le 0.001</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: No for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.8</annotation></semantics></math>: there <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)^n = (-0.2)^n</annotation></semantics></math>, so every term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(n + 1)(0.2)^n}{2^{n-1}}</annotation></semantics></math> is positive; the series does not alternate and the alternating series error bound does not apply
accept: "all the terms are positive at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.8</annotation></semantics></math>"

parts.sample: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1.2</annotation></semantics></math> the terms of the Taylor series are <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(-1)^n (n + 1)(0.2)^n}{2^{n-1}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (-1)^n \cdot 2(n + 1)(0.1)^n</annotation></semantics></math>. They alternate in sign; their sizes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.06</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.008</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.001</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2, 0.4, 0.06, 0.008, 0.001, \ldots</annotation></semantics></math> decrease, since the ratio of consecutive sizes is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{n + 2}{n + 1}(0.1) < 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and approach 0. So the alternating series error bound applies, and since <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_3(1.2)</annotation></semantics></math> is the sum of the terms for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1.2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|h(1.2) - P_3(1.2)\right| \le</annotation></semantics></math> the size of the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n = 4</annotation></semantics></math> term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.001</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{5(0.2)^4}{2^3} = 0.001</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0.8</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)^n = (-0.2)^n</annotation></semantics></math>, so each term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(-1)^n (n + 1)(-0.2)^n}{2^{n-1}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{(n + 1)(0.2)^n}{2^{n-1}} > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The series does not alternate there, so the alternating series error bound cannot be used; the Lagrange error bound still can.
